evals.expected_output: A coherent diagnostic system design with an evidence-driven investigation strategy, bounded experiments and version-bound conclusions. The sample demonstrates both architecture and nontrivial diagnostic reasoning rather than a one-off patch.
expectations: [system-composition] Define how a PR and CI evidence become an investigation, bounded checks and a reviewable report, using the existing platform capabilities and keeping execution and user decision boundaries explicit.

[diagnostic-strategy] Explain how observations yield competing or coexisting hypotheses, how the next check is selected to distinguish them, how outcomes revise confidence and remaining work, and when to stop. A generic read-log/ask-LLM/rerun pipeline or a static error-to-fix lookup is insufficient.

[sample-discrimination] Use the sample to distinguish the recorded engine rejection from optional-native warnings and unrelated baseline DNS failure. Treat the API shape and cursor-version issues as separate supported concerns; distinguish observed failures from plausible consequences and do not claim production incompatibility is established.

[experiment-selection] Provide concrete proposed checks with their controlled SHA/patch/environment, the uncertainty each could resolve, and relevant alternative outcomes. Respect 6 checks/15 minutes and do not invent completed results. No fixed bisection, causality framework or experimental order is required.

[evidence-identity] Tie conclusions and reuse to exact source revision, patch, environment and tested scope; explain handling new PR revisions or new evidence. Do not turn mock-only green tests or a failed baseline install into broad compatibility proof.
